findings.title: Smoke result dropped when Run errors
findings.message: If a.Run returns an error before the smoke goroutine finishes, run returns without waiting; also if smokeCheck never completes the watchdog kills the process. More importantly, smokeCheck mutates workbench from a.Do while the main thread also uses it, relying on Do for sync; but the polling loop calls a.Do after Close may fail, acceptable. The result channel is only read if Run succeeded, leaking otherwise.
findings.suggestion: Read the result on error paths too, or ignore since buffered; ensure smoke failure is not masked when Run returns an error.
findings.evidence: go func() { result <- smokeCheck(a, ref, m); a.Close() }()

findings.title: Objects lacking a feature are always hidden
findings.message: Hidden bug check: when the 'move' reorder is applied, features are shifted with append/copy on a cloned slice. That is fine, but the visibility toggle only affects Objects while refresh hides bodies by feature marker, so a body with no feature entry is always invisible (active[id] defaults to false).
findings.suggestion: Treat objects without a feature as active: only hide when a feature exists and its index >= Marker.

finding.title: Stale featureID after delete
finding.message: The smoke test and timeline timing aside, deleteSelected filters Features in place via s.Features[:0] on a clone; this is safe, but Undo's 'before' snapshot is shared only through clone, fine. However the 'move' handler leaves m.featureID stale after delete, and featureChange 'select' on a feature whose Object was removed is harmless.
finding.suggestion: Reset m.featureID when its feature is deleted.
